name: Prompt & Context Engineering
tagline: Design the instructions, examples and context that make AI models reliable at real tasks.

overview.summary: Prompt engineering is the skill of getting consistent, high-quality results from AI models by writing clear instructions, giving good examples, and supplying the right context (documents, data, tool results). In 2025 the industry started calling the broader version 'context engineering': deciding exactly what information a model sees at each step. Honest note: standalone 'Prompt Engineer' job titles are becoming rarer — the skill is now expected inside many roles (AI engineer, content, support operations, product, marketing, data). That makes it one of the most useful entry points into AI work, especially for non-programmers.
whyTrending: LinkedIn reported in its Jobs on the Rise 2026 coverage that most hiring leaders now prefer candidates who are skilled with AI tools over more experienced peers without those skills.

Companies deploying AI assistants and agents need people who can write system prompts, build evaluation sets and fix failure cases — often called AI trainers, AI content specialists or LLM evaluators.
The work shifted from clever one-line prompts to engineering the full context: retrieval, memory, tool descriptions and examples — a skill that transfers to AI engineering.
It has the lowest barrier to entry of any AI field: you can start with a free chat tool and a spreadsheet of test cases.

roles.description: Writes and maintains system prompts, tool descriptions and retrieval setups for AI features, and tests them against evaluation sets.

roles.title: AI Trainer / LLM Evaluator
roles.description: Creates high-quality examples, rates model outputs and writes rubrics that are used to evaluate or fine-tune models.

roles.title: Conversational Designer
roles.description: Designs the personality, flows and fallback behaviour of chatbots and voice assistants.

roles.title: AI Content & Automation Specialist
roles.description: Uses AI tools and no-code automation (Zapier, Make, n8n) to speed up marketing, support or operations workflows.

roles.title: AI Solutions Consultant

stack.note: Most listings ask for strong writing plus evidence of evaluation work. Basic Python or an automation tool turns this from a 'skill' into a role you can be hired for.

interview.question: What makes a good prompt?
interview.answer: Clear goal, relevant context, explicit constraints, the desired output format and — when useful — examples. It should be specific enough that a smart new colleague could follow it.

interview.question: What is few-shot prompting?
interview.answer: Including a few input–output examples in the prompt so the model copies the pattern, format and style.

interview.question: What is context engineering?
interview.answer: Deciding everything the model sees at each step — instructions, retrieved documents, tool results, memory and examples — and keeping it relevant and compact so the model performs reliably.

interview.question: How do you know if a prompt change is an improvement?
interview.answer: Test it on a fixed evaluation set with clear scoring before and after, rather than judging from one or two examples.

interview.question: How do you reduce hallucinations?
interview.answer: Ground the model with retrieved sources, ask it to cite them, allow it to say 'I don't know', lower temperature for factual tasks and verify outputs.

interview.question: What is prompt chaining?
interview.answer: Splitting a complex task into a sequence of smaller prompts where each output feeds the next, which improves reliability and makes debugging easier.

interview.question: What is prompt injection?
interview.answer: An attack where text in user input or retrieved documents tries to override your instructions. Mitigate by separating data from instructions, limiting tool permissions and validating outputs.

interview.question: When would you choose fine-tuning over prompting?
interview.answer: When you need a consistent style or format at scale, have many good examples, and prompting alone is too long, costly or inconsistent.

interview.question: What does temperature control?
interview.answer: Randomness of the output. Low values give focused, repeatable answers; higher values give more varied, creative ones.

interview.question: How would you train a non-technical team to use AI safely?
interview.answer: Short hands-on sessions with real tasks, a shared prompt library, clear rules on confidential data, and a habit of verifying outputs before use.

demandNotes.bangladesh: Growing as a freelancing and agency skill (content, support, automation). Few full-time 'prompt engineer' posts — combine it with marketing, support, data or development.
demandNotes.remote: Steady demand for AI trainers, evaluators and automation builders; strongest when paired with a domain (law, medicine, finance, coding) or a language such as Bangla.
demandNotes.global: Skill demand is very high but the standalone title is shrinking; employers fold it into AI engineering, product and operations roles.
